## Problem `--all-release-tags --release-version-from-package --date-from-version` names the window **after the latest tag** after `package.json`'s version. Between releases, `package.json` still holds the version that was just tagged and published, so items that close after that release are rendered **inside the already-published release's section**. `CHANGELOG.md` on main then claims that the published npm version contains changes it does not have. When an item lands in a section that used to be item-less, that section's dependency notes also disappear, because item-less sections keep Dependencies and sections with items drop them. So regenerating rewrites the content of a section that was already released. ## Observed in the fleet (2026-11-12) - **pm-github#233, after merging release v2026.11.12.** The released section `## 2026.11.12 - 2026-11-12` held only `### Dependencies` (Bump jscpd #232). On the PR branch the same heading now also lists the PR's own pending item under `### Fixed`. To keep the dependency line, the agent added `--dependency-updates` to the repo's generator. - **pm-context#225, a closure PR.** `package.json` is still 2026.11.1, a prepared release that never published. The 11-12 fix is rendered as `## 2026.11.1 - 2026-11-01`, and that section's ten dependency entries are gone. ## Expected - When the package version already has a matching release tag (`v` or ``), the window after that tag renders as `## Unreleased`, or is omitted, not as another `## ` section, and the tagged section's content stays exactly what the tag window produces. - `--release-version-from-package` names the pending window only when that version is **not** tagged yet, which is the release-preparation case. - `--check` stays stable across a release and the following closure regenerations, so they never rewrite a published section. ## Acceptance - In a fixture whose tag `v2.0.0` has one dependency-only commit, with `package.json` 2.0.0 and one item closed after the tag: the output has `## Unreleased` with the item, and `## 2.0.0` keeps only its dependency line. - With `package.json` 2.0.1 untagged (preparation), the same item renders under `## 2.0.1 - `. - The released section's bytes are unchanged between the two runs. --- ### GitHub comments (2) > **@coderabbitai[bot]** (2026-11-12T22:23:25Z) > > > > >

Drop into our [discord](https://discord.gg/coderabbit)! > **@unbraind** (2026-11-16T20:05:07Z) > > More fleet evidence, 2026-11-16, and a second facet: an item whose `release` field names an old version. > > Nine closure PRs from the 2026-11-14 in-progress sweep close items that were delivered in an already published release. The items carry that release assignment, so `--respect-item-release` renders them inside the published section even after merging current main, where `package.json` already names a newer pending version. Each time, the published section loses its Dependencies bullets, because "sections with items drop Dependencies": > > | PR | Published section | Bullets removed / added | > |---|---|---| > | pm-linear#223 | 2026.11.11 | −5 / +1 | > | pm-ts-starter#211 | 2026.11.10 | −5 / +1 | > | pm-starter#209 | 2026.11.9 | −4 / +1 | > | pm-todos#199 | 2026.11.11 | −6 / +1 | > | pm-presets#218 | 2026.11.10 | −4 / +2 | > | pm-jira#207 | 2026.11.5, 2026.11.7 | −1 / +2 | > | pm-memory#70 | 2026.11.13 | bullet order reversed | > | pm-hypothesis#32 | 2026.10.25 (on npm, untagged) | +1 | > | pm-swarm#76 | 2026.11.11 | −2 | > > `changelog:check` demands exact generator output, so a repository cannot keep the published notes by hand. Every late closure of a delivered item therefore either rewrites a released section or never closes. These items are stuck in `in_progress` until this is fixed. > > Proposal, so that published sections stay stable: > 1. A section's Dependencies list depends only on the commits in its tag window, never on whether the section also has items. A section that gains a late-closed item keeps its dependency bullets. > 2. To avoid churning every existing item-bearing section on the upgrade, apply (1) only to sections where a dependency bullet would otherwise disappear. Alternatively, ship (1) behind an opt-in flag that the fleet enables with one regeneration per repository. > 3. Contract test: closing an item assigned to a tagged release adds exactly its own bullet and removes nothing. >
Pending items render inside the already-published release section when package.json still holds the tagged version
